results.title: Where do locals go in Chicago when they want a fun night out? | SPIN
results.content:
The best interactive entertainment venues in Chicago are places where the activity itself is the social anchor, giving groups something to do together rather than just sit and scroll. Top options include ping pong clubs, bowling alleys with a bar program, escape rooms, and comedy clubs, all of which give people a reason to engage with each other rather than the room.

Interactive venues have become one of the most popular things to do tonight in Chicago because they solve a real problem: traditional bars can feel passive, especially for groups who do not know each other well or want to do more than drink. An activity creates a shared experience, breaks the ice naturally, and gives the night a shape and a story. [...] 1. Book ahead for popular venues, especially on weekends. Many social venues near me searches in Chicago turn up spots that fill up by Thursday for Saturday night.
2. Choose a neighborhood and stay in it. Moving a group of eight people across the city between stops kills momentum fast.
3. Pick an activity that works for your group's dynamic. Competitive types love head-to-head games; more casual groups do better with something collaborative or low-stakes.
4. Confirm dietary needs in advance if food is part of the plan, and look for menus with genuine variety.
5. Set a loose start time and a hard meeting point so the group does not spend the first 45 minutes trying to find each other.

## When is the best time to go out in Chicago for the full experience? [...] One pattern worth knowing: venues that specialize in shareable, snackable food tend to work better for entertainment nights than those built around formal plated meals. When you are moving between an activity and a table, you want food that travels with the conversation rather than demanding everyone sit still for an hour. Small plates, loaded fries, flatbreads, and grazing boards are the formats that keep the energy up.

On the drinks side, look for venues that go beyond a basic well bar. Seasonally inspired cocktails, a solid local craft beer selection, and spirit-free options signal that the venue takes hospitality seriously and caters to a range of preferences across a group.

results.content:
Cleveland’s known for its blue-collar roots, so hard work is part of our nature. In that same vein, we know a thing or two about letting off some steam when the workday is over.

So, when visitors ask, “What are some things to do near me tonight?” our answer usually starts somewhere along Cleveland’s east bank of the Cuyahoga River in an area known as The Flats. Whether you’re a non-drinker who just wants some amazing waterfront dining or a perennial rug-cutter who’s into bottle service and clubs, the revived East Bank of The Flats is the place for fun with friends in Cleveland. [...] Closer to the center of Downtown Cleveland there’s also the East Fourth Street Entertainment District, featuring Hilarities comedy club, music at the House of Blues and stylish cocktails at Society Lounge. There’s also Playhouse Square, which is almost always buzzing with big-name performances, Broadway shows and dinner/drink havens, while the Historic Warehouse District offers a bevy of thumping clubs and unique dining experiences. But Downtown is just the start...

Finding a good time is easy in The Land. How you turn it up is up to you.

results.title: Chicago Nightlife Guide: What to Do in Chicago at Night - Thrillist
results.content:
Photo by Ranvestel Photographic

In terms of sleepless cities, Chicago may not be a notorious night owl like Las Vegas or New York, but America’s third largest city certainly knows how to keep things interesting after dark—in totally G-rated ways. By day, it’s a mighty metropolis famed for its soaring architecture, A-list festivals, and buzzy restaurants. After dark, though, the city transforms, offering a whole new slate of entertainment for all walks of life. Whether your idea of “nightlife” includes family-centric activities around sunset, a nightcap overlooking Lake Michigan, a twilight snack, or last-call on the dance floor, there’s something in Chicago for just about everyone. So, no matter what your bedtime is, here are 25 things to do in Chicago after dark. [...] Fulton Market

Look out for: The fanciest nightcaps you’ve ever sipped  
If your idea of late-night snacks includes Vietnamese duck wings and $2,000 worth of caviar, then After is the after-dinner bar of your dreams. Designed as a kind of decadent digestif for its adjacent sister restaurant, the Michelin-starred tasting menu temple Ever, you’d expect nothing less from one of the most acclaimed chefs in town. The posh lounge is the handiwork of chef Curtis Duffy and Michael Muser, who’ve put together a gorgeous space with equally gorgeous drinks and small plates. Along with a curated menu of cheffy nibbles, the deep cocktail list offers something for everyone—including fig-infused Sazeracs, coconut water Mai Tais, and truffled Espresso Martinis. The lounge is open until midnight. [...] Late-night tunes is a bucket list essential in Chicago, and while there are always new venues popping up all over town, there’s always something nostalgic about revisiting an old haunt. For the most heartwarming, intoxicating blast from the past, head to the Empty Bottle, a Ukrainian Village institution that’s been pumping out live shows and dirt-cheap beer since 1992. Today, the gritty corner bar is still as popular as ever, the drinks are practically as cheap as ever, and many shows are still free. Its dark and cozy confines make it particularly apt for a winter night, and as an added bonus, barflies can order Sicilian-style pizza from adjoining Pizza Friendly Pizza, whose menu is curated by Michelin-starred chef Noah Sandoval of Oriole.
